hypotheses.justification: `ha` follows from `[IsHausdorff (Ideal.span {a}) V]` together with `[IsDomain V]`. `V` is a valuation domain, so it is a local ring. Suppose `a ∉ maximalIdeal V`. Then `IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal` (MaximalIdeal/Basic.lean:83) says `a` is a unit, and `Ideal.span_singleton_eq_top` gives `Ideal.span {a} = ⊤`. The Hausdorff instance then becomes `IsHausdorff ⊤ V`, and `IsHausdorff.subsingleton` (AdicCompletion/Basic.lean:182) makes `V` a subsingleton. That contradicts `Nontrivial V`, which comes from `IsDomain V`. So the new proof first recovers `ha` with `by_contra h; haveI := (Ideal.span_singleton_eq_top.mpr (IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal.mp h) ▸ ‹IsHausdorff (Ideal.span {a}) V›).subsingleton; exact not_subsingleton V` (or something close), then runs the existing proof. `ha` is mentioned nowhere else in the statement. The converse fails: `[IsHausdorff]` does not follow from `ha`, because Mathlib's `IsHausdorff.of_isDomain` needs `IsNoetherianRing`, and valuation rings are not Noetherian in general.

The conclusion never mentions `K`. It only involves `V`, `a`, `AdicCompletion (Ideal.span {a}) V` and `P`. `K` is used only in the proof, to call `principalAdicCompletionPrimeSpectrumOrderIso K a ha0 ha`. Without `[IsFractionRing V K]`, the proof can call it with the canonical fraction field instead: `principalAdicCompletionPrimeSpectrumOrderIso (FractionRing V) a ha0 ha`. For a domain `V`, `FractionRing V` has standard Mathlib instances `Field`, `Algebra V (FractionRing V)` and `IsFractionRing V (FractionRing V)`. The definition is universe-polymorphic in `v`, so using `FractionRing V : Type u` is fine. The binders `K`, `[Field K]` and `[Algebra V K]` stay and simply go unused. Those three cannot be removed one at a time, because each is needed for a later binder to elaborate. Only `[IsFractionRing V K]` can be removed alone.
